page: Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by dual Intel Xeon 8375C processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 physical cores, 128 dedicated execution threads operating at a 3.5 GHz clock speed, and 54 MB of L3 cache. The platform is configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is provisioned via 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking is rated at a 50 Gbps baseline. The system contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high multi-threaded compute density and high memory throughput. The system attained a PassMark CPU score of 88191.68 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 124966.04, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. Memory bandwidth reaches 338.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 132.33 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database handling capabilities are reflected in 110.69 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operations results. Single-threaded benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core (1670.0) and compression tasks, sit within average mid-tier percentiles. Generative text generation on large language models shows typical CPU limitations, registering 2.79 tokens per second on 70B models.

Eliminating hypervisor overhead on bare-metal hardware allows direct access to memory channels and high-speed local NVMe volumes. The pairing of one terabyte of RAM with 7.6 TB of direct-attached solid-state storage minimizes storage latency bottlenecks. This configuration is engineered for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise in-memory caches such as Redis, relational and NoSQL databases, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput transaction processing systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 64-core Intel Xeon 8375C processors at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 128 dedicated execution threads. It is equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 RAM, 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 88191.68 and uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 338 GB/s. Memory-intensive execution is validated by 110.69 million Redis SET operations per second and robust database transaction scores. While single-threaded tasks and large-model generative AI token throughput show standard CPU constraints, the platform offers significant architectural efficiency for low-latency memory processing. AWS r6id.metal is suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, real-time analytics, and transactional data workloads demanding high local disk I/O.
